analyst_view.overall: Betis are 4th with 27 points and strong at La Cartuja, while Rayo are 16th with 12 points, have not won away in six and lost 0-1 at home to Valencia last weekend. Betis won 2-0 in Bratislava in the Champions League on Tuesday night and host Rayo at 14:00 on Saturday, a short turnaround with an early kick-off that the numbers do not see; the players with most minutes only did recovery work on Wednesday. Lo Celso's knee knock is now described as a contusion that is not serious and improving, and Ceballos and Morante, whom the numbers count as out, are also day-to-day, so Betis may have more of their midfield than the numbers assume. Rayo, under Beñat San José, are without Batalla and Luiz Felipe (counted), with Óscar Valentín still nursing a knee contusion and doubtful to travel. No referee named yet; the numbers already count the run of tight meetings between these sides lightly.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals, already about 5% lower on Betis's side for Ceballos and Morante being out, plus their quiet recent scoring and the tight past meetings with Rayo. Yesterday I trimmed for Lo Celso's knee, but the latest report says the knock is not serious and that Ceballos and Morante could also make it, which would undo part of what the numbers took off; against that, Betis come off a Champions League trip with a 14:00 Saturday kick-off. Those pull in opposite directions, so I drop my trim and stay at 2.4, with most of the goals expected from Betis since Rayo have scored little away.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.5 corners, with Betis's recent rise in corners (33 in six) already added. Betis attack wide through Abde and Antony and Rayo push their full-backs forward, with Pedrosa expected back at left-back, so a normal corner count fits. Nothing I found changes this, so I stay at 10.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.3 cards, with Rayo expected to take most of them; both sides' recent card counts and the past meetings are already counted. The referee has not been named yet, so his record can't be judged. Rayo away, sitting near the bottom, tend to defend deep and foul, which the numbers already reflect, so I stay at 5.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.0 shots, pushed up by strong recent shot counts on both sides (Rayo 104 in their last six), which they already add. I trim a little, to about 30.1: Betis played in Bratislava on Tuesday night and kick off at 14:00 on Saturday, so some rotation and a lower tempo are likely, and the numbers don't know about the midweek game. I made the trim smaller than yesterday because Lo Celso's knee problem now looks minor.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.4 shots on target, with recent accuracy and the missing Ceballos and Morante already counted. The midweek trip may cost a few shots, but Betis could also get Lo Celso and possibly Ceballos back, which would add quality to their chances, so I see no reason to move. Rayo's finishing away has been weak, which the numbers already know; I stay at 9.4.
